Neutrophil metabolic pathways

Neutrophil metabolic pathways. Glucose uptake via GLUT transporters fuels glycolysis for ATP generation and provides G6P for NADPH production through the PPP, supporting NOX-dependent ROS production. Glycogen cycling maintains intracellular glucose availability under nutrient-limiting conditions, with the final step of glycogenolysis mediated by ER-embedded G6Pase. Glycolytic intermediates drive the synthesis of cytoplasmic UDP-sugars and glycans, supplying substrates for protein glycosylation in the ER. Functional mitochondria contribute via the TCA cycle and OXPHOS, utilizing pyruvate, glutamine, fatty acids, and propionate-derived intermediates. In addition to ATP production, metabolic intermediates support various intracellular biosynthetic processes. Figure created with BioRender (BioRender.com)
